import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 921

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/921](https://www.erdosproblems.com/921)
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., Problems and results in chromatic graph theory. Proof Techniques in Graph
  Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
- [Ga63] Gallai, T., Kritische Graphen. I. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1963), 165-192.
- [KST84] Kierstead, H. A., Szemerédi, E. and Trotter, W. T., On coloring graphs with locally
  small chromatic number. Combinatorica (1984), 183-185.
-/

open Filter

namespace Erdos921

/--
Let $k\geq 4$ and let $f_k(n)$ be the largest $m$ such that there is a graph on $n$ vertices
with chromatic number $k$ in which every odd cycle has length $> m$.
Then
$$f_k(n) \asymp n^{\frac{1}{k-2}}.$$

A question of Erdős and Gallai.

Proved for all $k\geq 4$ by Kierstead, Szemerédi, and Trotter [KST84].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_921 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (k : ℕ), 4 ≤ k →
      ∃ (c₁ c₂ : ℝ), 0 < c₁ ∧ 0 < c₂ ∧
        (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
          (∃ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
            G.chromaticNumber = (k : ℕ∞) ∧
            ∀ l ∈ G.oddCycleLengths, c₁ * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / ((k : ℝ) - 2)) < (l : ℝ))) ∧
        (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
          ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
            G.chromaticNumber = (k : ℕ∞) →
            ∃ l ∈ G.oddCycleLengths, (l : ℝ) ≤ c₂ * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / ((k : ℝ) - 2))) := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos921

reformulations.difference: The theorem expresses the extremal growth claim through separate existential lower and universal upper bounds on odd-cycle lengths, rather than defining f_k(n) and asserting an asymp relation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For fixed k≥4 and n≥k, let g_k(n) be the maximum, over n-vertex k-chromatic graphs, of the shortest odd-cycle length. These graphs have odd cycles, and f_k(n)=g_k(n)−1≥2. The Lean conditions are exactly eventual bounds c₁ n^(1/(k−2)) < f_k(n)+1 ≤ c₂ n^(1/(k−2)). Since f_k(n) ≤ f_k(n)+1 ≤ 2f_k(n), these are equivalent to two-sided positive-constant bounds on f_k(n), after adjusting constants. The two eventual conditions can share a threshold by taking the maximum of their thresholds. A sorry-free Lean proof in /workspace/review/reformulation.lean establishes the equivalence for the exact graph predicates, using the defining IsGreatest characterization of f_k.

reformulations.difference: The upper bound quantifies over graphs with chromatic number exactly k. Erdős's original paper phrases the bound as sufficiently large odd girth forcing chromatic number less than k, thus also addressing graphs with chromatic number greater than k.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every finite graph with chromatic number at least k contains a spanning subgraph with chromatic number exactly k: delete edges one at a time, noting that one deletion decreases chromatic number by at most one. The spanning subgraph has the same number of vertices and introduces no new cycles. Consequently the Lean upper bound supplies a suitably short odd cycle in the original graph as well. The converse restriction to exactly k is immediate.

sources_consulted: Erdős, P., Problems and results in chromatic graph theory (1969), especially p. 31: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1969-13.pdf
